checks: Verified original fe4ccc381e7e406a at its declared digest, introduction and §§1–3, equations (1)–(8). The frozen statement retains the physical record identities only. The subsequent finite-knot replacement/reconstruction theorem and its external candidate are not invoked.

Compactness, convexity, and nesting of the hypograph give concave nonincreasing signed endpoints and nonnegative width. The top left limits are exactly the limiting endpoints by compactness, even for a plateau or singleton. At zero height, concavity and r(0)>0 imply every interior axial coordinate has positive height, forcing the right limits to be the base endpoints even if their heights vanish.

Changing variables x=±v in the point-mass term recovers |x|^(m−1)/2 and the second layer term adds (r(z)^(m−1)−|x|^(m−1))/2 for m≥2. For m=1 only the two moving boundary point masses are needed. Total layer mass per axial length is m v^(m−1).

Outside [−sv,sv], all or none of a transverse layer is captured, giving ±m v^(m−1)/2 after centering. Inside, one boundary atom is captured, canceling its half-mass baseline, and the continuous part gives (m−1)v^(m−2)z/(2s). Integrating this odd function gives the stated even primitive, matched at both endpoints. Evaluation at A and −B handles intervals on either side of zero, crossing zero, or collapsing at the top.

A−sv strictly decreases; the positive initial value and negative secant slope at any zero of A+sv imply strict negativity after that zero. The same reasoning holds for B and for the zero branch. Thus finitely many equality levels have no effect, even with plateau arms. Piecewise bounds on ∂t and ∂s dominate difference quotients by integrable v^(m−1) and v^m multiples.

Translation of a cutoff to ε takes the primitive arguments to A−ε and B+ε and leaves layer length fixed, giving the sum of the threshold derivatives with the stated sign. The line meets the interior at (0,0) and has at most two boundary points; slice differentiation in z is legitimate for almost every x with a common bounded support and bounded density. Graph length over x contributes exactly √(1+s²), canceled by the raw coarea divisor. On the line z=−sx, hence M=−sP′; the derivative of the inner kernel gives both coefficients and the outer contribution is zero.

At s=0 the interval positive length is A when both arms are nonnegative, A+B when B<0, and zero when A<0; the absolute-value formula covers all three and their boundaries. The direct section has length 2r(0), density r(0)^(m−1)/2 and zero first moment. The first arm zero before the top marks the last level containing z=0. On the stated branch cells the only arm-dependent moments for m≥2 are the three listed, and the omission of m−1 terms leaves only first moments of the arms for m=1.

Independent exact check used r(z)=1+z on [−1/2,1], s=1/4. Its B arm crosses +sv, zero, and −sv below R. Direct section and cap integration and exact piecewise inverse-arm integration agreed: (V,P,C,M)=(15/8,22/15,16/15,16/225) for m=1 and (21/8,1544/675,256/225,1024/10125) for m=2.

overlap.comparison: Defines the same planar interval-layer records for a positive concave homothetic profile, gives their direct coarea interpretation and zero-slope values, and averages over transverse radii. It does not give the signed inverse-height kernels or a finite list of signed-arm moments that determines them.

Computes the same physical cap/coarea/moment records via an energy formula for affine frusta only. That overlapping profile subclass does not imply the branch formulas for arbitrary continuous concave profiles.

readability: Read the signed endpoints as actual axial bounds −B and A; in particular a negative arm is not a negative interval width. For m=1 any value assigned to the density at a zero-width endpoint is immaterial to all integrals.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The signed-arm identities give the cap mass, raw coarea, and raw vertical section moment for the full stated profile class and all stated slopes, including zero slope, m=1, and sources below the maximum.
